reason: Intro. Names the film, states we've never seen it, no research. 14.5s, no housekeeping.

'I don't like not knowing' / 'Here's a fact for everybody: we don't know anything about this movie.' Establishes the cold-open premise in their own words and sets up every later called-it-early moment.
Theresa's story about being pulled over by a motorcycle cop lands directly over the film's opening traffic stop. Personal tangent, not a reaction to a beat, so film_beat stays null.

film_beat: Motorcycle cop pulls over Parnell's Malibu in the desert and is warned off the trunk.
reason: Setup for the vaporization. Short on purpose; ends on 'Give me the keys' so the payoff lands in its own segment after a hard break.

film_beat: The cop opens the trunk, is vaporized by the light inside, and leaves only smoking boots.
reason: ICONIC. The film's calling card. Reaction resolves over ~20s: confusion, then 'Boots were made for walking,' then 'just melted the shit out of that guy's body.' pip_circles so the trunk light owns the screen.

film_beat: Mr Humphries lectures Otto about how he spaces the cans; Otto tells him to fuck off, flips off the security guard and is fired.
reason: ICONIC. Sits on top of a 13-second silent reaction, and the dynamic is layered right on the beat: 'I space the cans. I'm the only one paying attention to anything spatial wise in this house.'
The folding argument. 'You don't like how I fold?' / 'I don't.' Planted here because it pays off 18 minutes later when Miss Magruder maces Bud.

film_beat: Bud cons Otto into driving a car for twenty-five bucks by claiming his pregnant wife is stranded.
reason: The recruitment beat plus the first 'it's like Men in Black' call, a theory that runs the whole cut.
Clean disagreement about old cars: 'I feel like the old cars are so cool looking' / 'No.' Escalates into whether their own car looks like everyone else's.

film_beat: Bud repossesses a car in front of its owner; Otto works out what the job actually is.
reason: 'I think he's a repo man' called a beat before the film confirms it. Short, and the title lands.
The boot tangent: 'I thought they put a wheel on it' / 'You mean the boot?' One of them not having the word for something the other has, which is the channel's bread and butter.

film_beat: Otto is handed a beer at the repo yard and told he's all right.
reason: Reaction moves off the film and onto each other: 'He's very soft spoken' / 'Unless he's losing a hockey game and then he yells like crazy.'

film_beat: Otto insists he'll never be a repo man; Bud tells him it's too late, he already is.
reason: Load-bearing for the story. Short by design, ends on 'Without even asking, he got a job.'

The running 'who is that guy' bit begins: 'Isn't that a guy that you know?' / 'The guy from Short Circuit?' / 'It's not.' / 'You know everything.' Neither of them lands on Tracey Walter, and it comes back at 3840.

Triggered by hearing 'People just explode. Natural causes,' but it becomes a claim about spontaneous combustion in St. Pete. Hosts fullscreen with the film audible is the honest layout: they're reacting to a line, not an image.
Converse / Nike / Michael Jordan tangent. 'Every movie we've watched in the 80s pretty much has had Converse in it' is a nice bit of channel continuity.

film_beat: Reverend Larry's telethon tells viewers to mortgage the house and sell the car; Otto eats out of a can labelled FOOD.
reason: ICONIC. The televangelist satire and the generic packaging in one shot, with the curtains-and-flamingos rant running on top of it. Best example in the cut of a tangent that improves a film beat instead of replacing it.
'Do you think our daughter looks at us like that?' / 'That we look like zombies?' plus 'God forbid we talk in a movie theater.' Self-aware and short.

film_beat: Otto asks for the $1,000 his parents promised him; they've given it to the telethon and are too stoned to care.
reason: They clock the joint before the film points at it, then disagree about whether the parents are Rastafarians. Story-critical: it's why Otto has nothing to lose.

The cut-off sleeves argument. 'I'm gonna start cutting the sleeves off my shirts' / 'You wanna be a single man again, I feel' / 'He did that' / 'I don't think he did anything, the costume person did it.' Longest pure tangent in the cut and it earns the length.

film_beat: Bud tells Otto to dress like a detective, then: 'Only an asshole gets killed for a car.'
reason: ICONIC line, and it's the setup for Bud's death at 5126. Their fourth-wall correction ('third wall or whatever' / 'I think it's the fourth wall') sits right on it.

film_beat: Bud recites the Repo Code and follows it with 'Ordinary fucking people, I hate 'em.'
reason: ICONIC, two of them. The reaction is the dynamic: 'You think you live by a code?' / 'No, no code' / 'Thou shalt not kill' / 'That's the ten commandments.'

film_beat: Bud and Otto stop at a liquor store stocked entirely with generic DRINK, BEER and pickled eggs.
reason: ICONIC. The generic-products gag is one of the film's signature images and it pays off twice later ('the beer says beer on it', 'Tasty-os'). 'I love all the generic stuff' opens the segment.

film_beat: Otto cracks his neck loudly in the LA River.
reason: Small beat, big reaction. 'Did you hear it?' / 'That was so loud' / 'I wonder if it came through on the microphone' / 'Like he gave himself a chiropractic adjustment.'

film_beat: Otto and Bud race the Rodriguez brothers through the concrete LA River.
reason: Disagreement on the beat: 'That would be a blast, I'd be all in on that' / 'No, I'm good.'

film_beat: After the chase Bud delivers the film's thesis: 'Repo man's always intense.'
reason: ICONIC. The line the film is known for, and one of them repeats it back immediately. Ends on 'I just like to scream.' pip_circles because the chase needs the frame.
'Just reminds me of Grand Theft Auto' into 'when we went to LA it felt like that in some places.' Their own experience, not the film's.
'I'm hungry. Can I have a snack?' / 'You want something out of our snack bucket?' Small domestic beat that sets up the callback at 2278.

film_beat: Miss Magruder maces Bud and Lite when they try to repossess her car.
reason: Pays off the folding argument from 476: 'I need a mace thing' / 'Why do you need to mace me? What did I do?' / 'You didn't fold your clothes.'

film_beat: Bud repossesses a millionaire's Cadillac outside a laundromat.
reason: 'What millionaire you know goes to the laundromat?' / 'We must own the laundromat.' Reaction to the beat rather than narration of it.

film_beat: Otto picks Leila up off the street; she's unimpressed and gets in anyway.
reason: 'Rule number one as a woman is never get in a car with some dude.' Reads the scene against itself.

film_beat: Leila shows Otto a photo of four dead aliens and explains the Malibu's trunk.
reason: Major plot reveal, and the 'I told you there was aliens' payoff for the theory started at 613. pip_circles for the photograph.
Clean split: 'I would love to see aliens' / 'I'm pass on that' / 'What if they come at you and want to eat your head?' / 'They'll eat it either way.'

film_beat: A $20,000 bounty goes out on the 1964 Chevy Malibu.
reason: Required for coherence: this is the engine of the rest of the film. They connect it themselves: 'That's the Malibu, so that must have the alien in it.'

film_beat: Miller's cosmic unconsciousness speech: the lattice of coincidence and the plate of shrimp.
reason: ICONIC. The most quoted scene in the film. They sit through it almost silently, then answer the monologue with 'You love the plate of shrimp' / 'I do, I love shrimp.'

film_beat: Miller on Bermuda triangles, UFOs and how the Mayans invented television.
reason: 'The Mayans invented television?' / 'They might've, they invented the calendar' / 'Science with Teresa.' One of them defending an absurd claim on the spot.
S'mores over a burning car. 'You'd like fire, you know more about fire' / 'I'm a little too health conscious for burning chemicals.' Also serves as a hard break inside a long Miller stretch.

film_beat: Miller: 'The more you drive, the less intelligent you are.'
reason: ICONIC. Immediately weaponized: 'Oh, you're a stupid dad' / 'Thank you.'
'I feel like I have the longest snack of all time' / 'We've been eating it for half the movie' / 'Are you enjoying it?' / 'I am.' Callback to 1549 and a warm breather before the back half.
The raspberry beret exchange. One of them quoting Prince without realizing it, the other not getting the reference until it's spelled out. Pure standalone dynamic.

film_beat: Otto strips in the UFO cult office and propositions Leila.
reason: 'Talk about being a little forward' / 'You're not slick, dude' / 'She just walks in and this kid's in his underwear and she's totally cool with it.'
Reese's Pieces and Hoodsie cups. Straight 80s nostalgia, no film content, and it buys a hard break before the commies beat.

film_beat: Bud interrogates Otto about communism: 'I don't want no commies in my car. No Christians either.'
reason: ICONIC. Flagged: the reaction here is thin, one 'Everything's free in Russia?' and a 'False.' The line is the payload, so it's in regardless. Consider a punch-in or a caption in the edit.
Casting a bit part: 'Reminds me of what's-his-face, the Canadian guy' / 'Eugene Levy?' / 'The eyebrows' / 'That kid looks like Napoleon Dynamite.'

film_beat: Kevin the pump attendant offers to check the Malibu's trunk.
reason: Yelling at the screen: 'Please don't check the trunk. You don't wanna melt, you don't wanna be melted. You're gonna melt.' Calls back to the opening.

film_beat: The Rodriguez brothers distract Kevin and drive off with the Malibu.
reason: Major turn. They ID the brothers correctly after guessing wrong first, which is exactly the kind of beat that plays.
The scooter gang sets off a Vespa tangent: 'I'd be all in on a scooter' / 'You've always told me how much you want a Vespa.'
Tea and cookies, into a confident wrong call: 'It's a British movie.' Being wrong out loud is the whole format.

film_beat: Otto is jumped and beaten with a guitar case while a street preacher rants nearby.
reason: 'Yep, with a guitar case' and the introduction of the Skid Row Shaman, who they end up rooting for.

film_beat: Plettschner's war-record rant at Otto: three times decorated, five years in a slaughterhouse, ten years at Attica.
reason: Big film speech, and the reaction turns into 'I think my favorite guy is the shaman' / 'He's your people.'

film_beat: The Rodriguez brothers cook in the Malibu and decide to open the trunk.
reason: Called well ahead: 'Oh, boys, you're in trouble' / 'We're gonna see some melted shoes on the ground.' The prediction is wrong, which makes it better.
Whether cars had AC in the 80s, into crank windows and a million-degree car. Longest breather in the middle third and a needed hard break.
Mohawk tangent prompted by the punks on screen but entirely about him: 'I could see you sporting a mohawk' / 'Your hair would be so long it'd be really intense.'
'You wouldn't be catching me walking around over there.' Their actual trip to LA, tents and all. Standalone, and it earns its place.
Popcorn arrives. 'You're so loud with the popcorn' / 'You're so judgy.' Nine seconds of setup for a two-word punchline.

film_beat: Lite pulls a gun and fires into a house to take a car; Otto refuses to get in.
reason: Turning point for Otto and the reaction tracks it: 'You don't mess with the repo man' / 'It's part of the job, white boy.'

film_beat: Lite reveals he was firing blanks.
reason: Short, and the payload is laughter rather than a line.

film_beat: Agents snatch Leila off the street.
reason: 'I called it from the beginning, that it was the men in black.' The theory from 613 finally confirmed.

film_beat: Rogersz interrogates Leila: 'Illegal aliens?' / 'No, silly. Extraterrestrials.'
reason: 'See, told you' / 'Tell me what?' The disagreement is about who called it, which is better than the reveal itself.

film_beat: Miller announces that John Wayne was gay and explains about the two-way mirrors in Brentwood.
reason: ICONIC. Flagged: the reaction is laughter and nothing else, no line. Still in, because the beat is what people come for.

film_beat: Otto's punk friends meet Agent Rogersz, poke her metal hand, and Duke declares 'let's go do some crimes.'
reason: ICONIC, two beats in one scene. 'Kiss my metal hand' and then one of them repeating the crimes line back at the screen.

film_beat: Duke opens the Malibu's trunk and burns his hand.
reason: ICONIC. Long silent stretch through the open, which is the point. 'Here comes some melted shoozies' just before is the best prediction in the cut.

film_beat: Archie looks in the trunk and is vaporized down to a skeleton; Duke: 'Let's go get sushi and not pay.'
reason: ICONIC. 'I love that you see the skeleton,' and the first Tarantino call, which pays off at 4931.
'This is a very odd movie' / 'But it is keeping us entertained, isn't it?' Honest mid-film verdict, twelve seconds, no film needed.

film_beat: Three separate crews converge on the Malibu at once.
reason: Keeps the plot legible and contains the recurring complaint: 'Where are the actual police? I feel like there aren't any police.'

film_beat: The Rodriguez brothers turn out to own the car; Bud has to be held back.
reason: 'He's like one of those things where you're getting to fight and he's like, hold me back, hold me back.'
'Was he in Stargate?' The who-is-that-guy bit from 918 returns, still unresolved, with 'we're gonna do some research on these people.' Best long-range callback in the recording.

film_beat: Oly takes Bud off the job and then fires him outright.
reason: Story-critical and kept short so the knitting tangent can have its own segment.
'The cop is knitting' into 'Didn't you knit?' / 'I crocheted' / 'Never did it when I was with you' / 'I could have sworn you did.' A small factual dispute about their own history.

film_beat: A hazmat crew collects a body while a technician narrates into a recorder.
reason: 'I like that they're all in hazmat suits and they're just letting him walk around.' Keeps the alien-radiation thread visible.

film_beat: Otto is violently sick in the street after driving the Malibu.
reason: 'One thing I can't handle is barf.' Reaction to a beat, and it's the first sign the car is doing something to him.

film_beat: Parnell rhapsodises about radiation: everybody could stand a hundred chest X-rays a year.
reason: 'He's a conspiracy theorist.' Sets up the neutron bomb monologue after a hard break.

film_beat: Parnell reveals he designed the neutron bomb: destroys people, leaves buildings standing, fits in a suitcase.
reason: ICONIC. The film's central piece of exposition, and 'Mm, it's an interesting pick, Doug' lands right on top of 'eyes melt, skin explodes, everybody dead.'

film_beat: Parnell dies at the wheel; Otto pulls the body out and takes the Malibu.
reason: 'Maybe don't touch him' / 'Is he just gonna kick him out and take the thing?' / 'It's like a Weekend at Bernie's situation.'
What $20,000 was worth in the early 80s. Standalone, and it makes the bounty mean something to a viewer.

film_beat: At the yard party Oly's wife hangs all over Otto.
reason: 'They want like the young blood.' Short read of a scene the film doesn't explain.

film_beat: Duke asks Debbi to settle down and have his baby.
reason: 'They just watched some dude literally melt out of their shoes and they're just sitting here hanging out.' The observation is sharper than the scene.

film_beat: The liquor store holdup goes wrong and everyone is shot.
reason: 'Is everybody dead?' / 'That took an interesting turn.' Major beat, minimal narration.

film_beat: Dying Duke blames society; Otto tells him he's a white suburban punk just like him.
reason: ICONIC. The film's best-known exchange. 'This is a strange fucking movie' lands mid-speech and one of them repeats 'Society made me what I am' back.

film_beat: Marlene fights off the agents and Plettschner throws boiling coffee.
reason: 'She's like a James Bond girl, she's just coming out of nowhere.'

film_beat: Agent Rogersz tortures Otto for the Malibu's location; Leila is now one of them.
reason: 'She's been turned' and 'I don't know how this movie could end.' Both are reactions to the turn, not descriptions of it.

film_beat: Otto shoots his way out of the hospital while Reverend Larry broadcasts an appeal for the stolen Malibu.
reason: 'Now he's got a submachine gun' / 'They all got Uzis?' / 'This movie's ridiculous,' then a long laugh over Larry's toll-free number.
Both claiming the Tarantino observation at once: 'I told you' / 'Did you not hear, I said that' / 'I didn't hear you say Tarantino.' Best pure two-hander in the back half.

film_beat: Bud pulls a gun on Otto demanding the Malibu.
reason: 'Buck, buck, buck' over Bud's clucking, then 'He has risen and he is gone.'

film_beat: Otto slips away and breaks into a car with a slim jim.
reason: 'That's a good way to break into a car' / 'I don't even use those things anymore.' Short, and it keeps the geography clear.

film_beat: Radio reports freak hail over downtown; the Malibu is now glowing green.
reason: Contains the running complaint about the absent police and military, then 'It looks like those stars you'd stick on your ceiling.'

film_beat: Bud finds Otto in the glowing Malibu and proposes a sixty-forty split.
reason: 'Told you, he was in on it, he knows.' The punchline about who gets the sixty plays on their laugh.

film_beat: Bud refuses to back down, throws 'only an asshole gets killed over a car' back at Otto, and is shot in the street.
reason: ICONIC. Pays off the line planted at 1241. Reaction is two flat 'okay's and silence, which is the right reaction and worth keeping as is.

film_beat: A news crew approaches the Malibu and hits a force field.
reason: 'You picked quite a movie, Doug.' Direct address to the person who chose the film, on a beat.

film_beat: A priest and the government team try to approach the car; another man is vaporised.
reason: 'Send the lady with the metal hand to open it' / 'Is it a rabbi and a Catholic priest?' / 'Oh, Jesus zapped it.'

film_beat: Miller climbs into the glowing Malibu and says he's going for a little spin.
reason: ICONIC. 'He's the alien' / 'Oh, the shaman's in the car' / 'See, I told you,' then 'I thought he doesn't wanna drive,' which is the joke the film is making.

film_beat: Otto gets in; Leila begs him not to go and he tells her to fuck off.
reason: 'They're both aliens' / 'I'd be staying the heck out of there.' Keeps the last turn readable.

film_beat: The Malibu lifts off and flies over Los Angeles.
reason: ICONIC. The ending, and the best sustained reaction in the recording: 'If that fucking car flies right now, I'm gonna lose it' / 'Told you' / 'It flies' / 'This is you losing it?' repeated four times.

film_beat: Miller's closing line: 'This is intense.' / 'The life of a repo man is always intense.'
reason: ICONIC. The film's first line about repo men returns as its last. One of them repeats it back, mangled, which is a good place to end the film content.
Outro. 'That was fucked up' / 'It was slow until the end when it just went off the fucking rails' / 'That was bananas' / 'I have no words.' Ends on 'the last little bit was the cream of the crop.'
